knowledge:
- key_parameters: pairs=An ExpressionSet object used to store or append imported signal intensity data ;; chips=A character vector of chip identifiers to be mapped to sample names ;; file=Path to a tab-delimited sample key file containing CHIP_ID and SAMPLE columns ;; ndf.file=Path to the NimbleGen Design Format (.ndf) file ;; ngd.file=Path to the NimbleGen Gene Description (.ngd) file ;; center=Logical value indicating whether to mean-center data before calculating prototypes ;; num.bins=Number of bins to use for quantile normalization ;; num.steps=Number of steps to use for quantile normalization ;; mode=The normalization mode, such as "discrete" ;; element=The ExpressionSet assayData element to extract (e.g., "exprs" for MspI, "exprs2" for HpaII) ;; feature.group=The featureData variable name used to group probes for summarization ;; trim=The fraction of observations to be trimmed from each end of the data before the mean is computed
- alternatives: The documentation mentions the RMA (Robust Multi-array Average) method as a conceptually similar quantile normalization approach, but the package's quantileNormalize() function is specifically tailored for intra-array normalization across density-dependent sliding windows of size-sorted data to correct for LM-PCR size bias.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing DNA methylation data generated using the HELP (HpaII tiny fragment Enrichment by Ligation-mediated PCR) assay protocol on Roche NimbleGen microarrays.
- pitfalls: The LM-PCR step in the HELP assay introduces a significant fragment size bias that must be corrected using quantile normalization. Background noise must be carefully accounted for by identifying "failed" probes (where MspI and HpaII signals are indistinguishable from random probe background) and treating them separately during the normalization process.

workflows.name: help_methylation_pipeline
workflows.intent: Import, normalize, summarize, and visualize DNA methylation data from HELP assay microarrays.
workflows.stages: 1. Import raw pair files using readPairs() ;; 2. Map chip IDs to human-readable sample names using readSampleKey() ;; 3. Load design and genomic feature information using readDesign() ;; 4. Calculate probe properties such as melting temperature (calcTm) and GC content (calcGC) ;; 5. Perform quality control using prototype calculation (calcPrototype), spatial chip plotting (plotChip), and fragment size vs. intensity plotting (plotFeature) ;; 6. Identify background noise thresholds using random probes ;; 7. Perform single-sample quantile normalization using quantileNormalize() to correct for fragment size bias ;; 8. Summarize probe-level data to fragment-level data using combineData() ;; 9. Visualize sample relationships using pairwise correlation plots (plotPairs)
workflows.code:
msp1.files <- dir(data.path, pattern="532[._]pair", full.names=TRUE)
hpa2.files <- dir(data.path, pattern="635[._]pair", full.names=TRUE)
N <- length(msp1.files)
for (i in 1:N) {
	if (i == 1) {
		pairs <- readPairs(msp1.files[i],hpa2.files[i])
	}
	else {
		pairs <- readPairs(msp1.files[i],hpa2.files[i],pairs)
	}
}
chips <- sub("[_.]*532[_.]*pair.*","",basename(msp1.files))
samplekey <- file.path(data.path, "sample.key.txt")
chips <- readSampleKey(file=samplekey,chips=chips)
sampleNames(pairs) <- chips
ndf.file <- file.path(data.path, "HELP.ndf.txt")
ngd.file <- file.path(data.path, "HELP.ngd.txt")
pairs <- readDesign(ndf.file, ngd.file, pairs)
calcTm("ATCTAGGAAGATTTAGAGAGGCAATGTGTCATTTAGCATCTAATTTTACC")
calcTm(getFeatures(pairs,"SEQUENCE")[1:4])
calcGC("ATCTAGGAAGATTTAGAGAGGCAATGTGTCATTTAGCATCTAATTTTACC")
calcGC(getFeatures(pairs,"SEQUENCE")[1:4])
getSamples(pairs)[1:4,]
calcPrototype(pairs,center=FALSE)[1:4]
plotChip(pairs, sample="Brain2")
exprs(pairs) <- log2(exprs(pairs))
exprs2(pairs) <- log2(exprs2(pairs))
plotFeature(pairs[,"Brain2"],cex=0.5)
rand <- which(getFeatures(pairs, "TYPE")=="RAND")
msp.rand <- getSamples(pairs, element="exprs")[rand,]
hpa.rand <- getSamples(pairs, element="exprs2")[rand,]
msp.rand.med <- apply(msp.rand, 2, median)
msp.rand.mad <- apply(msp.rand, 2, mad)
hpa.rand.med <- apply(hpa.rand, 2, median)
hpa.rand.mad <- apply(hpa.rand, 2, mad)
msp.fail <- msp.rand.med + 2.5*msp.rand.mad
hpa.fail <- hpa.rand.med + 2.5*hpa.rand.mad
hpa.meth <- apply(hpa.rand, 2, quantile, 0.99)
norand <- which(getFeatures(pairs, "TYPE")=="DATA")
size <- as.numeric(getFeatures(pairs, "SIZE"))[norand]
msp <- getSamples(pairs, "Brain2", element="exprs")[norand]
hpa <- getSamples(pairs, "Brain2", element="exprs2")[norand]
nofail <- which(msp>msp.fail["Brain2"] | hpa>hpa.fail["Brain2"])
msp.norm <- msp
msp.norm[nofail] <- quantileNormalize(msp[nofail],size[nofail])
meth <- which(msp>msp.fail["Brain2"] & hpa<=hpa.meth["Brain2"])
hpa.norm <- hpa
hpa.norm[meth] <- quantileNormalize(hpa[meth],size[meth])
nometh <- which(hpa>hpa.meth["Brain2"])
hpa.norm[nometh] <- quantileNormalize(hpa[nometh],size[nometh])
pairs.norm <- pairs
exprs(pairs.norm)[norand, "Brain2"] <- msp.norm
exprs2(pairs.norm)[norand, "Brain2"] <- hpa.norm
data <- getSamples(pairs,element="exprs2")
seqids <- getFeatures(pairs,'SEQ_ID')
weight <- getSamples(pairs,element="exprs")
combineData(data, seqids, weight, trim=0.2)[1:5,]
combineData(pairs, feature.group='SEQ_ID', trim=0.2)[1:5,]
plotPairs(pairs,element="exprs2")
